title: SoftBank Group deepens AI bets as Vision Fund weighs exits
body:
SoftBank Group Corp. is expanding its artificial intelligence investments even as Vision Fund managers prepare selective exits from mature portfolio companies.

Chief Executive Masayoshi Son said the firm remains "super optimistic" about AI infrastructure and semiconductor demand, linking the thesis to SoftBank's stake in Arm Holdings.

Analysts noted SoftBank's balance sheet flexibility improved after earlier asset sales, but currency swings and interest costs remain a watchpoint for equity investors.

The company did not announce a new mega-fund raise in the latest briefing.

title: Arm Holdings growth tied to smartphone rebound and AI accelerators
body:
Arm Holdings reported stronger royalty momentum as smartphone volumes stabilized and customers designed AI accelerators around Arm architectures.

SoftBank Group remains Arm's controlling shareholder. Investors watched commentary from Masayoshi Son about Arm's role in SoftBank's broader AI strategy.

Competitors in custom silicon continue to pressure pricing, but Arm's licensing model still benefits from broad ecosystem adoption.

title: ByteDance navigates regulatory scrutiny while expanding enterprise AI tools
body:
ByteDance is investing in enterprise AI productivity tools even as regulators in multiple jurisdictions review its consumer apps.

Company executives said advertising revenue remained resilient, while management emphasized compliance investments.

Separately, competitors in short-video and cloud services continued aggressive hiring in large language model teams.

title: Deutsche Bank pushes wealth and corporate banking as restructuring continues
body:
Deutsche Bank outlined progress on its restructuring plan, highlighting wealth management inflows and tighter cost controls in investment banking.

Executives said net interest income remained sensitive to the European rate path. The lender reiterated capital targets and downside risks from commercial real estate exposures.

Note: some secondary wires misspelled the bank as 'Deutche Bank' in earlier alerts, creating entity-resolution noise in archives.

title: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority increases allocations to private credit
body:
Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) is increasing exposure to private credit strategies amid higher-for-longer rate expectations.

People familiar with the matter said the sovereign wealth fund is pairing private credit with selective infrastructure investments while remaining cautious on crowded venture valuations.

ADIA did not publicly disclose exact ticket sizes.

title: Private credit market trends: fundraising slows but deployment stays active
body:
Fundraising in private credit cooled compared with 2021-2022 peaks, yet deployment into direct lending remained active as banks retreated from some mid-market loans.

Investors including sovereign wealth funds and insurers sought floating-rate structures. Risks include documentation quality, refinancing walls, and correlated defaults in a sharper slowdown.

Market participants said transparency and covenant quality are becoming differentiators among managers.

title: Jerome Powell signals patience on rate cuts as inflation progress stalls
body:
Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said policymakers can be patient on further rate cuts if inflation progress stalls, while still describing the labor market as broadly solid.

Powell emphasized data dependence and avoided committing to a preset path. Markets trimmed near-term cut expectations after the remarks.

Regional Fed presidents offered mixed views on the timing of easing.

title: Christine Lagarde says ECB must stay alert to services inflation
body:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said services inflation remains sticky even as goods prices ease, arguing the ECB must stay alert.

Lagarde linked wage dynamics in services to the persistence of underlying inflation. Analysts said the remarks reduced odds of an aggressive cutting cycle.

title: Brazil and deforestation rates 2025: policy shifts under scrutiny
body:
Brazil's 2025 deforestation indicators in the Amazon are being watched by investors assessing commodity supply-chain risk and EU deforestation regulation exposure.

Officials pointed to enforcement campaigns, while NGOs argued illegal clearing persists in frontier municipalities.

Agribusiness exporters said compliance documentation costs are rising for shipments into Europe.

title: EU AI Act compliance deadlines push boards to map high-risk systems
body:
Companies operating in Europe are accelerating EU AI Act compliance programs, focusing on high-risk system inventories, transparency duties, and vendor diligence.

Legal advisers said documentation and post-market monitoring will be operational bottlenecks. U.S. technology firms argued for clarity on general-purpose AI obligations.

Procurement teams are adding contractual clauses on model evaluation and incident reporting.

title: Patagonia Inc. expands repair programs amid outdoor apparel competition
body:
Patagonia Inc. expanded garment repair and resale programs as outdoor apparel rivals compete on sustainability claims.

The company reiterated its activist brand posture while investing in supply-chain traceability. Market share battles intensified with legacy sportswear brands entering premium outdoor categories.

title: Andy Jassy outlines AWS growth strategy around AI infrastructure demand
body:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said AWS growth is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure demand, including custom chips and higher-margin software services layered on cloud usage.

Jassy argued that enterprise migrations remain early and that AI training and inference workloads favor hyperscale providers with power and networking capacity.

Investors focused on capital expenditure intensity and the competitive response from Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud.

title: Larry Fink's annual letter to CEOs focuses on retirement and private markets
body:
BlackRock CEO Larry Fink's annual letter to CEOs emphasized retirement system reform and wider access to private markets for individual investors.

Fink argued democratization of alternatives must be paired with education and fee transparency. The letter also addressed infrastructure investment needs and AI productivity.

Critics said private-market access for retail investors raises liquidity and valuation concerns.

title: Electric vehicles and battery recycling attract policy support and capital
body:
Electric vehicles and battery recycling are drawing policy support in the U.S., EU, and Asia as governments try to secure critical minerals and reduce waste.

Startups and automakers are forming joint ventures for black-mass processing. Analysts warned that feedstock availability and chemistry shifts could strand some early facilities.

Automakers said recycled content mandates are becoming a procurement requirement.

title: The silent crisis of teacher shortages hits workforce pipelines
body:
Education officials described teacher shortages as a silent crisis affecting STEM pipelines and long-run workforce quality.

Retention, compensation, and burnout dominate policy debates. Employers in technology and healthcare said talent bottlenecks begin years earlier in secondary education systems.

Comparative international data showed uneven vacancy rates across regions.

title: Nigeria's business climate: FX reforms, inflation, and investor caution
body:
Nigeria's business climate in 2025 remains shaped by foreign-exchange reforms, sticky inflation, and selective investor caution.

Corporates reported improved access to dollars versus crisis peaks, but pricing volatility complicated planning. Political risk and power reliability continue to weigh on manufacturing investment.

Banks highlighted opportunities in consumer fintech while watching asset quality.

title: Apple Inc. retail traffic stabilizes in major U.S. malls
body:
Apple Inc. reported stabilizing retail traffic in major U.S. shopping centers during the holiday period, according to mall operators.

This article is about Apple consumer retail footfall, not SoftBank, ByteDance, or European banks. It exists as a hard negative for unrelated entity queries.

title: Jamie Dimon on the future of the economy warns on fiscal trajectory
body:
JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that the future of the economy hinges on fiscal trajectory, geopolitical risk, and AI-driven productivity that may arrive unevenly.

Dimon said consumers remain resilient but that geopolitical shocks could reprice risk assets quickly. He also commented on bank capital rules and market liquidity.

Investors parsed the remarks for signals on credit costs and dealmaking.
